common_name: ProCut Orange Sunflower (Single-Stem Golden-Orange Cut Flower)

planting.note: Direct sow after the last frost once soil is above 60°F, and repeat sowings every 1-2 weeks through midsummer for a continuous cut-flower supply.

directions: Sow seeds 0.5 inch deep on tight 6-9 inch spacing in full sun so plants channel all their growth into a single unbranched stem topped with one flower. ProCut Orange is the vivid golden-orange member of the industry-standard ProCut single-stem series, distinguished by a warmer, deeper hue than the yellow and lemon shades in the line, on a plant that flowers uniformly and all at once about 55-65 days after sowing. Because the flowers are pollen-free, they hold up well in mixed bouquets without dropping pollen on fabric or other blooms. Stake or support plantings in exposed sites, and harvest as petals just begin to unfurl for the longest vase life.
sources: Association of Specialty Cut Flower Growers

common_name: ProCut Bicolor Sunflower (Single-Stem Red-and-Gold Cut Flower)

planting.note: Direct sow after the last frost once soil is above 60°F, succession sowing every 1-2 weeks for staggered harvests since the whole planting blooms together.

directions: Plant on close 6-9 inch spacing in full sun; like other members of the ProCut series, Bicolor puts its energy into a single strong stem and one flower rather than branching. Its petals open deep red at the base and shade to gold at the tips, giving each bloom a two-toned, painterly look that stands out among the mostly solid-color sunflowers used in bouquets. The pollen-free flowers won't shed onto tablecloths or clothing, and uniform stem height and bloom timing make the crop easy to plan for market bunches. Harvest when petals have just begun to unfurl but the center disk is still tight, and cut in the cool morning for the best vase life.

common_name: SunRich Orange Sunflower (Pollen-Free Single-Stem Orange Cut Flower)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost when soil is above 60°F; succession sow every 1-2 weeks through summer since the crop matures all at once.

directions: Direct sow 0.5 inch deep on 6-9 inch spacing in full sun; SunRich Orange grows as a single unbranched stem bred for uniform height and bloom timing, the traits that make the SunRich line a favorite of commercial growers. The rich, deep-orange petals surround a dark center disk and hold their color well in the field and in the vase, offering a bolder alternative to the paler golds and lemons elsewhere in the series. Because the flowers are pollen-free, they're a clean choice for mixed arrangements and won't stain fabric. Plan on harvesting the entire planting within a narrow window, roughly 55-65 days after sowing, and cut when petals have just started to open for maximum vase life.
sources: Association of Specialty Cut Flower Growers

common_name: Chianti Sunflower (Deep Burgundy-Red Branching Pollen-Free Sunflower)

planting.note: Direct sow after all danger of frost has passed, spacing plants to allow branching, or succession sow every 2-3 weeks for continuous blooms.

directions: Sow directly in full sun after the soil has warmed, giving plants 12-18 inches of space so their side branches can develop fully. Chianti is prized for its unusually dark, wine-red petals that read almost black-red in bright light, a striking departure from the orange-reds of most branching sunflower cultivars. Because it branches freely, a single plant produces many flowers in succession over several weeks rather than one big bloom all at once, extending the cutting season from one sowing. The pollen-free flowers stay tidy in mixed bouquets and won't shed onto tablecloths, and deadheading spent blooms encourages the plant to keep producing new side shoots into fall.

common_name: Valentine Sunflower (Pale Lemon-Yellow Branching Pollen-Free Sunflower)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost once soil has warmed; space plants well to let the branching habit develop for a longer bloom season.

directions: Plant in full sun with 12-18 inches between plants so the multi-branching habit has room to fill out. Valentine produces pale, creamy lemon-yellow petals around a chocolate-brown center, a soft pastel look that fits cottage-garden and wedding-style arrangements better than the saturated golds and oranges of most sunflowers. Its branching habit means each plant yields a steady succession of medium-sized blooms over many weeks rather than a single large flush, and the pollen-free flowers keep vases and tablecloths clean. Regular cutting or deadheading of spent flowers keeps the plant producing new buds until frost.

common_name: Pacino Sunflower (Compact Dwarf Branching Pot Sunflower)

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after the last frost; Pacino stays compact enough to grow in large containers as well as garden beds.

directions: Sow in full sun in average garden soil or a large container with drainage; Pacino stays a compact 14-20 inches tall, far shorter than typical branching sunflowers, while still producing multiple golden-yellow blooms per plant. Its dwarf, bushy habit makes it one of the few sunflower cultivars genuinely suited to patio pots and small-space gardens without staking. Flowers open earlier than most sunflower types, often within about seven to eight weeks of sowing, giving a quick, reliable display for container plantings or edging a bed. Deadhead spent flowers to keep the compact plants tidy and encourage additional side blooms through summer.
